scenes.title: Lunch break
scenes.summary: Tell a coworker what you had for lunch.

turns.message: Hey! What did you have for lunch? 🍽️
turns.hint: You had roast chicken.
turns.reply: I had roast chicken for lunch.
wrongReplies: I took roast chicken in the lunch.
I ate a roast chicken lunching.
turns.note: Use “had” to say what you ate or drank.

turns.message: Nice! A whole chicken or just one part?
turns.hint: Just the white meat.
wrongReplies: Just the chicken chest.
Just the chicken white part.
turns.note: A chicken breast is the lean white-meat cut from a chicken.

turns.message: Did it come with anything?
turns.hint: A small salad served with the main dish.
turns.reply: It came with a side salad.
wrongReplies: It came with salad at the side of it.
It came with a lateral salad.
turns.note: A side salad is a small salad served alongside the main dish.

turns.message: Any rice?
turns.hint: Rice cooked with broth and seasonings.
wrongReplies: Yeah, some rice with broth style.
Yeah, some seasoned rice soup.
turns.note: Rice pilaf is rice cooked with broth and often aromatics or seasonings.

turns.message: Sounds healthy 😄 What did you drink?
turns.hint: You chose mango juice.
wrongReplies: I took a mango juice.
I drank a juice of mangoes.
turns.note: Use “had” for a drink you chose with a meal, too.

scenes.closing: Okay, now I’m hungry again 😂 See you at the meeting!

scenes.title: The new restaurant
scenes.summary: Say how a meal tasted and recommend the place.

turns.message: So, how was that new restaurant?
turns.hint: You enjoyed it.
wrongReplies: It was very deliciously.
It was with good flavor.
turns.note: A simple, natural way to say you enjoyed something.

turns.message: What did you order?
turns.hint: Tacos with finely chopped beef.
turns.reply: I had tacos with ground beef.
wrongReplies: I had tacos with floor beef.
I had tacos with beef powder.
turns.note: In American English, “ground beef” is beef minced into small pieces.

turns.message: I heard their food is really hot 🌶️
turns.hint: It had a bit of heat, but not too much.
wrongReplies: It was small spicy.
It had few of spicy.
turns.note: “A little” softens an adjective and means “somewhat.”

turns.message: And the sauce?
turns.hint: It was both sugary and salty.
wrongReplies: It was sweet and salty flavorly.
It was sugar and meat taste.
turns.note: “Savory” describes a rich, salty flavor rather than a sweet one.

turns.message: What was the best thing you had?
turns.hint: The tacos.
wrongReplies: The tacos were the most like for me.
I liked tacos in a favorite way.
turns.note: Use “favorite” to name the thing you liked most.

turns.message: Hmm, maybe I should go.
turns.hint: Recommend it in a casual way.
wrongReplies: You must test it some time.
You should taste it one day sometime.
turns.note: A casual recommendation for something the other person might enjoy.

scenes.closing: Okay, it’s on my list. Thanks! 🙌

scenes.title: Cooking class
scenes.summary: Name the ways beef is cooked.

turns.message: First dish! We cook the beef in hot oil until it’s brown. What do we call it?
turns.hint: It’s cooked in hot oil.
wrongReplies: It’s beef frying.
It’s beef cooked in the fry.
turns.note: “Fried” describes food cooked in hot oil or fat.

turns.message: Now look at this slice. It’s very thin. What kind of steak is it?
turns.hint: A thin slice of beef.
wrongReplies: It’s a steak cut in thinly.
It’s a small thickness of beef.
turns.note: A thin-cut steak is a thin slice of beef prepared as a steak.

turns.message: We cook it in a skillet with just a little oil. How do we describe that?
turns.hint: A pan and a small amount of oil.
turns.reply: It’s pan-fried in a little oil.
wrongReplies: It’s pan-cooked by fryingly.
It’s fried inside the pan oil.
turns.note: “Pan-fried” means cooked in a pan with a small amount of oil or fat.

turns.message: Last dish: beef chunks cooked slowly in liquid for two hours. How was it prepared?
turns.hint: Cooked slowly in liquid until soft.
turns.reply: It was stewed in a rich sauce.
wrongReplies: It was swimming on a sauce.
It was cooked in a stewly way.
turns.note: “Stewed” describes food cooked slowly in liquid.

scenes.closing: Excellent work, everyone! Time to eat 🍴

scenes.title: Backyard barbecue
scenes.summary: Describe grilled and smoked food from a cookout.

turns.message: Saw your photos from Saturday! What did you guys eat?

image.alt: Grilled steak served with roasted vegetables.

turns.hint: Steak cooked on an outdoor grill.
turns.reply: We had grilled steak for dinner.
wrongReplies: We had steak grilledly for dinner.
We had steak from the outdoor oven bars.
turns.note: “Grilled” describes food cooked on a grill over direct heat.

turns.message: And these? They look amazing 🤤

image.alt: A rack of ribs cooking on a barbecue grill.

turns.hint: Ribs cooked slowly in wood smoke.
wrongReplies: We had ribs with smoking.
We had smoky ribs porks.
turns.note: “Smoked” describes meat cooked slowly in wood smoke for flavor.

turns.message: How long did they take?
turns.hint: Low heat for a long time.
turns.reply: Hours! They were smoked low and slow.
wrongReplies: Hours! They were smoked lowly and slowly.
Hours! They were smoked with a low speed.
turns.note: “Low and slow” is a casual way to describe barbecue cooked at low heat for a long time.

turns.message: Did you make anything else?
turns.hint: Beef so soft you could cut it with a fork.
turns.reply: Some slow-cooked beef. It was fork-tender.
wrongReplies: Some slow-cooked beef. It was tender by a fork.
Some slow-cooked beef. The fork became soft.
turns.note: “Fork-tender” describes food soft enough to cut with a fork.

turns.message: How do you get beef that soft without a smoker?
turns.hint: Brown it, then cook it slowly with a little liquid.
turns.reply: You braise it until it’s tender.
wrongReplies: You braisedly make it tender.
You boil it quickly until it’s tender.
turns.note: “Braise” means to brown meat first, then cook it slowly with a small amount of liquid.

scenes.closing: Next time, invite me! 😄 I’ll bring dessert.

scenes.title: Comfort food
scenes.summary: Talk about soups, stews, and creamy pasta.

turns.message: It’s so cold today 🥶 What did you have for lunch?
turns.hint: A bowl of soup made with beef ribs.
turns.reply: I had a bowl of beef rib soup.
wrongReplies: I had a soup of ribs beef.
I took beef ribs in a liquid bowl.
turns.note: This plainly describes a soup made with beef ribs.

turns.message: Yum. Was it good?
turns.hint: The liquid had a deep, salty, satisfying flavor.
turns.reply: The broth was rich and savory.
wrongReplies: The soup water was big and salty flavor.
The broth was savoryly richful.
turns.note: “Broth” is the flavorful liquid in a soup.

turns.message: I made this last night. Guess what it is!

image.alt: A bowl of beef stew with chunks of meat and vegetables.

turns.hint: Meat and vegetables in a thick, filling dish.
wrongReplies: A strong meat vegetables souping?
A stew with very much heart?
turns.note: “Hearty” describes a filling, substantial meal.

turns.message: Yes! Tomorrow I’m making this. Do you know what it’s called?

image.alt: A plate of creamy fettuccine Alfredo topped with parsley.

turns.hint: Flat ribbon pasta with a creamy sauce.
wrongReplies: That’s Alfredo fettuccine pasta sauce.
That’s flat noodles with the Alfredo on.
turns.note: Fettuccine is a flat, ribbon-shaped pasta often served with Alfredo sauce.

turns.message: What if I forget the name of the pasta?
turns.hint: Describe it in a general way.
turns.reply: Just say pasta with Alfredo sauce.
wrongReplies: Just say pasta with the sauce Alfredo.
Just say noodles and Alfredo in separate.
turns.note: Use a general description when you don’t know the exact pasta shape.

turns.message: And how would you describe the sauce?
turns.hint: Smooth, full of flavor, and made with cream.
wrongReplies: It’s cream and richness.
It’s smoothly creamful.
turns.note: “Creamy” describes a smooth texture. “Rich” describes a full, buttery flavor.
